problems.title: Lagged doses give incorrect gradients in coupled PK/PD solvers
problems.summary: The coupled PK/PD solver loses the contribution of the start time when differentiating the step following a lagged dose. The amount can be correct while its lag derivative is wrong.

draft.title: A lagged dose gives a spurious derivative in a constant-slope PD compartment
draft.body:
In Torsten Math develop at `bb8266ea`, call `pmx_solve_onecpt_rk45` with one extra PD state. Give the extra state initial value zero and an autonomous right-hand side returning the length-one vector `[1]`, independent of PK and parameters. Use θ = [10, 80, 1.2], unit bioavailability for all three compartments and compartment lags [L, 0, 0], with L a reverse-mode variable initialized to 0.35. Give a single 100-unit depot bolus at time 0, then observe at time 1. Use no infusion, repeat or steady-state initialization.

Differentiate the PD amount `y(2, 1)` with respect to L. Its value is 1 and Torsten returns a derivative of 1. For any L strictly between 0 and 1 the solution is L + (1 − L) = 1. Its derivative must be zero, including at L = 0.35. This example places the observation away from the event.

Preserving the derivative of the interval length across the event restores the cancellation. The same coupled step is used in the one- and two-compartment RK45 and BDF solvers. The [native reproducer and isolated patch results](https://github.com/nsiccha/torsten_math/blob/5726aad1124698cd2e2343bd47c1258a6d138043/dogfood-index.json) include the full C++ call.

problems.title: Repeated RATE-defined infusions disagree with steady-state initialization
problems.summary: When bioavailability differs from one, the transient schedule scales the rate and keeps its original duration. The steady-state solver keeps the rate and changes the duration. The two schedules agree on total dose but give different compartment amounts.

draft.title: RATE-defined dosing with fractional bioavailability gives two periodic solutions
draft.body:
In Torsten Math develop at `bb8266ea`, use `pmx_solve_onecpt` with CL = 10, V = 80 and ka = 1.2. Give 1200 units into the depot at 150 units/hour every 12 hours. Set depot bioavailability to 0.8 and all lags to zero. Compare the depot amount at the start of a dose under two schedules: initialize it with `ss = 1` at time 0, or initialize empty at −600 hours and repeat the same dose up to time 0. Read the amount at time 0 after that dose has started.

Steady-state initialization gives 0.150748. Repeated transient dosing gives 0.822919. With 960 units absorbed, the specified rate of 150 should last 6.4 hours. For duration d = 6.4, the expected periodic trough is (150/ka) × (1 − exp(−ka·d)) × exp(−ka·(12−d)) / (1 − exp(−ka·12)) = 0.150748. The transient solver spreads the 960 units over 8 hours instead.

Using the effective amount to schedule the infusion end also makes this event depend on bioavailability when computing gradients. The [native reproducer and isolated patch results](https://github.com/nsiccha/torsten_math/blob/5726aad1124698cd2e2343bd47c1258a6d138043/dogfood-index.json) give the two schedules in C++.

problems.title: Torsten ODE models can lose the state of their right-hand side
problems.summary: The event model factory passes the right-hand side by value. The model's stream adaptor retained a reference to that local copy after the factory returned. The adaptor now owns its copy for the lifetime of the model.

draft.title: ODE models should retain their right-hand-side functor after construction
draft.body:
In Torsten Math develop at `bb8266ea`, the event model factory constructs a PKODEModel with its own by-value copy of the right-hand-side functor. The model stores an ode_rhs_ostream_adaptor whose functor member refers to that copy. When construction returns, the reference is dangling. Stateful C++ right-hand sides need their stored parameters to remain valid for every later evaluation during the solve.

The adaptor can own the functor by value. The [single-header fix](https://github.com/nsiccha/torsten_math/commit/94c7d7472379412df5a6dfe6badc20ae3c41113b) applies directly to that upstream revision. It can be taken independently of support for user-supplied Jacobians.

problems.title: Chains stop when pmx_solve_rk45 runs out of steps
problems.summary: When pmx_solve_rk45 needs more than max_num_steps steps, boost's no_progress_error, a std::runtime_error, reaches Stan unchanged. Stan's samplers reject a proposal on std::domain_error and end the chain on any other exception, so a stiff proposal early in warmup stops the chain. The embedded Torsten integrator now reports the spent step budget as std::domain_error. Torsten v0.92.1 makes the same change upstream (metrumresearchgroup/Torsten 2b8db0eb, tag torsten_v0.92.1); metrumresearchgroup/torsten_math develop does not have it yet.

Torsten v0.92.1 repairs it upstream more broadly: its steady-state solves rethrow every failure as std::domain_error (metrumresearchgroup/Torsten 2b8db0eb, tag torsten_v0.92.1); metrumresearchgroup/torsten_math develop does not have it yet.

problems.title: Hand a thread's reverse-mode memory back to the operating system
problems.summary: Feature. recover_memory() keeps every block of the autodiff arena and the storage of the variable lists, so a long-lived thread holds the memory of its largest gradient for as long as it lives. The C++ functions release_memory() and stack_alloc::release_pages() hand that physical memory back to the system while keeping it allocated for the next gradient. BridgeStan's bs_release_memory calls them.

problems.title: Array categorical_lpmf and multinomial_lpmf give NaN gradients at a zero probability that no outcome selects
problems.summary: The reverse-mode gradient of categorical_lpmf for an array of outcomes is NaN whenever the probability vector has an entry that is exactly zero, even when no outcome selects it. The value is correct and the scalar overload gives the correct gradient. multinomial_lpmf does the same for a zero count at a zero probability. Exact zeros appear when a probability underflows, as in a softmax with a very negative logit, and the NaN then reaches every parameter the simplex depends on. Upstream develop has this behaviour.

draft.title: Array categorical_lpmf and multinomial_lpmf return NaN gradients when an unobserved category has probability zero

commits.title: Keep unobserved zero probabilities out of categorical and multinomial gradients

fix.why_together: One commit on upstream develop: both densities and their regression tests. The two functions fail for the same reason, a term with zero weight whose reverse pass divides zero by zero. On the dogfood branch the same change is the commit written on the v5.3.0-based solver branch plus the merge that adapts its one multinomial line to develop's lmultiply. The four changed files are byte-identical on both.
